Use it only for a text field that no dedicated tool sets; call_action and the state tools should handle normal edits. Returns the window, the typed text and the target element.

text.description: Text to type; Unicode characters are sent as key events.

ref.description: Element ref from the latest ui_tree or dialogs result.

query.description: Text, tooltip, actionId or objectName to find an on-screen element.

window.description: Window index or title substring (default: focused/main window).

replace.description: Clear the field before typing (default false).

release_focus.description: Drop keyboard focus afterwards so shortcuts reach Cascadeur again.

settle_ms.description: Milliseconds to wait for the UI to update before returning (default 150).

name: ui_set_property
description: Last resort: Set a QML property on an element (for example checked, value, text or currentIndex). Use it only when no dedicated tool or action exists: set_view_mode, set_ghosts, set_trajectories, set_silhouette and set_surface cover the display state. It bypasses input handlers. Returns ok, the value before and the value after.

ref.description: Element ref from the latest ui_tree or dialogs result.

name.description: QML property name, e.g. checked, value or text.

value.description: New property value (string, number, boolean or null).

name: ui_invoke
description: Last resort: Invoke a no-argument QML method or signal on an element, for example 'clicked', 'toggle', 'open' or 'close'. Use it only when the behavior has no dedicated tool or Cascadeur action; prefer call_action when the action has an actionId. Returns ok and the element details.

ref.description: Element ref from the latest ui_tree or dialogs result.

method.description: No-argument QML method or signal name, e.g. clicked or toggle.

name: dialogs
description: List visible dialogs/popups and secondary windows with their texts and button refs. Use it to check that a tool left no dialog open, or to find a prompt that needs an answer. Returns dialogs (kind, window index, type, texts, buttons with refs) and a hint to press a button with ui_click(ref=...); refreshing this list resets the ui_tree refs.

name: list_actions
description: List Cascadeur action keys (actionId) found in the live UI, for example 'Commands.Rig mode.On', with labels. Use it when no dedicated tool exists for an operation, then trigger the key with call_action. Returns actions (actionId, label, on_screen); actions of tools that have never been opened may be missing.

query.description: Only actions whose actionId contains this text.

include_hidden.description: Include actions of hidden windows (default true).

name: call_action
description: Trigger a Cascadeur action by key through ActionManager.call_action, exactly like its toolbar button or menu item. Use a dedicated tool first when one exists (set_pose, set_key, select_objects, ...); call_action is for actions that have no wrapper. Use list_actions to discover keys. Returns the called key.

key.description: Cascadeur actionId from list_actions, e.g. 'Commands.Rig mode.On'.

settle_ms.description: Milliseconds to wait for the UI to update before returning (default 150).

name: render_video
description: Render the animation timeline to an MP4 with Cascadeur's own encoder, through its official Export video window (File.Export.Video...), as a background job: returns a job_id immediately and get_job reports progress and the result. Use it to produce the final video after checking the motion with render_contact_sheet; do not screenshot frames or use an external ffmpeg. The whole animation is rendered unless start/end narrow the range. By default the camera is fitted to the union of the whole motion so a moving character stays in view, the display switches to the clean View mode (a solid shaded surface with no controller points, joints, boxes, trajectories or ghosts, and silhouette off), and the range, camera and display settings are restored afterwards; keep_overlays=true keeps the viewport's display instead. camera_preset also accepts current (keep the viewport camera) or front/back/left/right/top/three_quarter views. path must be absolute and end in .mp4; an existing file is only replaced with overwrite=true. width/height are pixels; samples selects the window's render quality (1 or less=LOW, 2-4=MEDIUM, more=HIGH; omitted=MEDIUM, 4 samples). The window's progress is reported and cancel_job presses its Stop button. Cascadeur must not be minimized. Returns the file path, byte size, encoded frame count, duration, fps and what was restored.

path.description: Absolute output path ending in .mp4 (default: a new file under %TEMP%).

start.description: First frame of the interval (default: the animation's first frame).

end.description: Last frame of the interval, inclusive (default: the animation's last frame).

samples.description: Render-quality selector: 1 or less=LOW, 2-4=MEDIUM, more=HIGH; omitted=MEDIUM (4 samples). The Export video window has no exact sample-count setting.

camera_preset.description: auto (default) fits the whole motion; current keeps the viewport camera; front/back/left/right/top/three_quarter fit the whole motion from that view.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at path (default false).

keep_overlays.description: true keeps the viewport's display (controller points, joints, ghosts, trajectories, silhouette) in the output; default false renders the clean View display.

name: render_image_sequence
description: Render the animation timeline to a folder of image files with Cascadeur's own renderer, through its official Export video window's IMAGE FILES mode, as a background job. Use it when a video is not needed or when the frames should be processed later; render_video makes the MP4. The whole animation is rendered unless start/end narrow the range; the same whole-motion camera, clean View display and restoration as render_video apply (keep_overlays=true keeps the viewport's display). folder must be an absolute path to a missing or empty folder (a new folder under %TEMP% is used by default); an existing folder with files is refused so old and new frames cannot mix. width/height are pixels; samples selects the window's render quality (1 or less=LOW, 2-4=MEDIUM, more=HIGH; omitted=MEDIUM, 4 samples). Returns a job_id; get_job reports progress and the resulting folder, file count and byte size. Cancel with cancel_job (it presses the dialog's Stop).

folder.description: Absolute destination folder (missing or empty; default: a new folder under %TEMP%).

start.description: First frame of the interval (default: the animation's first frame).

end.description: Last frame of the interval, inclusive (default: the animation's last frame).

samples.description: Render-quality selector: 1 or less=LOW, 2-4=MEDIUM, more=HIGH; omitted=MEDIUM (4 samples). The Export video window has no exact sample-count setting.

camera_preset.description: auto (default) fits the whole motion; current keeps the viewport camera; front/back/left/right/top/three_quarter fit the whole motion from that view.

keep_overlays.description: true keeps the viewport's display (controller points, joints, ghosts, trajectories, silhouette) in the output; default false renders the clean View display.

name: screenshot
description: Last resort: Capture a Cascadeur window (or one element by ref) as an image. Use render_image to see the 3D scene and render_contact_sheet to inspect a motion; screenshot is only for the interface itself (a widget, menu or dialog). window_units_per_pixel converts image pixels to the window coordinates used by ui_click x/y. Returns image content plus metadata (window title/size, image size, crop rectangle and scale); restore=true un-minimizes the window first.

window.description: Window index or title substring (default: focused/main window).

ref.description: Element ref from the latest ui_tree or dialogs result.

restore.description: Un-minimize the window first (a minimized window renders nothing).

name: project_point
description: Last resort: Project scene objects by name to main-window coordinates in the 3D viewport, for the last-resort ui_click/ui_drag tools. Use set_pose to move control points, select_objects to select them and the camera tools for normal work; this only computes coordinates. Uses the viewport camera and a 30 degree vertical FOV (verified for Cascadeur 2026.2.3). Returns each object's world position, depth, window x/y and whether it is on screen.

names.description: Exact scene object names to project, e.g. ['mixamorig:LeftHand_MainPoint']. Aliases such as left_hand are not resolved; list_controllers gives the names.

fov_deg.description: Vertical field of view in degrees (default 30, measured for Cascadeur 2026.2.3).
